note: Owns browser-side agent tools on a TYPO3 frontend. Backend MCP, built-in browser AI, and schema.org are adjacent but separate surfaces.

evals.prompt: Make the search and contact journey on this TYPO3 14 website available to browser agents through WebMCP.
Add document.modelContext tools to our TYPO3 sitepackage and test them in Chrome.
Can native Chrome WebMCP safely expose our TYPO3 news filters and frontend forms?
Audit whether this TYPO3 frontend is agent-ready and which WebMCP tools it should publish.
Our TYPO3 FAQ content element needs FAQPage JSON-LD for search engines.
evals.note: Search entity markup is not a browser tool.

evals.prompt: Make our existing TYPO3 contact form meet WCAG 2.2 AA and fix its keyboard focus.
Add an AI writing assistant inside the TYPO3 backend for our editors.
evals.note: A backend LLM assistant is not browser-side frontend WebMCP.

evals.prompt: This old example uses navigator.modelContext and provideContext. Copy it into our TYPO3 v14 site.
evals.expected_output: Checks the current living specification, targets document.modelContext/registerTool for new code, and treats the older surface only as an explicit compatibility path.
assertions: Identifies the current document.modelContext surface
Records WebMCP as experimental and rechecks browser support
Keeps unsupported-browser behavior as a tested progressive enhancement
Does not introduce a floating polyfill or CDN relay implicitly

evals.prompt: Install a TYPO3 WebMCP extension and its analytics dashboard so we do not have to write sitepackage code.
evals.expected_output: Declines the package and backend-MCP path, implements the browser-native API in the existing sitepackage/Vite build, and keeps analytics absent.
assertions: Uses document.modelContext directly without a TYPO3 WebMCP extension
Keeps implementation in a dedicated project-owned Vite entry
Reuses existing human-facing services and endpoints
Requires a Git rollback reference for the P14 code mutation
Introduces no analytics, relay, CDN runtime or backend MCP dependency

evals.prompt: Expose a tool that searches any URL, returns full editor comments, and submits the support form automatically.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the over-broad tool, splits read-only and consequential behavior, allowlists same-origin sources, marks untrusted output, and keeps visible user confirmation before submission.
assertions: Rejects arbitrary URL fetching and hidden/private output
Uses minimal bounded inputs and outputs
Preserves FE access, CSRF, rate limiting and server-side validation
Sets annotations according to actual mutation and output trust
Requires visible human confirmation for the consequential send

evals.prompt: Add WebMCP readiness to every TYPO3 upgrade without changing what visitors see during the core migration.
evals.expected_output: Inventories WebMCP in P00, preserves an existing surface in P10, and starts approved implementation only in P14 after Contract A, with both elevation branches joining before handover.
assertions: P00 inventories packages, APIs, headers, tools, endpoints and candidate journeys read-only
P10 parity is required only for a pre-existing surface and joins Contract A migration proof
New tools and dependencies stay outside Contract A
P14 requires intent approval, Git rollback and a green evidence loop
WebMCP and structured-data elevation converge through an explicit join before handover

evals.prompt: The inspector lists our tools and one search call worked. Mark the TYPO3 site WebMCP-ready.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the single-call claim and runs deterministic, security, session/language, fallback, human-interface, performance, accessibility, and repeated agent-selection evidence.
assertions: Tests valid, invalid, boundary, repeated and cancelled calls
Tests anonymous and materially different FE groups and languages
Tests injection, CSRF, rate limits, origins, hostile content and safe errors
Proves unsupported-browser fallback and unchanged human journeys
Runs repeated natural-language selection evals with browser and model versions
Re-runs component, axe and Lighthouse quality gates
